items.followUp: What is meant by a number system?

rubric.why: A number system uses symbols or digits to represent numbers.
rubric.description: Mentions the symbols or digits used.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying symbols or digits.

rubric.why: A number system represents numbers according to a defined method or rules.
rubric.description: Explains that the system represents numbers using a method or rules.

modelAnswer: A number system is a way of representing numbers using a set of symbols or digits and defined rules.

items.followUp: What is meant by non-volatile memory?

rubric.why: Volatile memory does not retain its contents when power is removed.
rubric.description: States what happens to the stored data when power is off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the data or contents are lost.

rubric.why: Identifies the condition causing data loss or gives a common example.
rubric.description: Mentions loss on power-off or identifies RAM as volatile memory.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory is temporary memory that loses its stored data when the power is switched off.
RAM is an example of volatile memory.

items.followUp: How many bits are there in a byte?

rubric.why: A byte is defined as a group of eight bits.
rubric.description: Defines a byte as eight bits.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct definition.

modelAnswer: A byte is a unit of data equal to 8 bits.

items.followUp: What is meant by booting a computer?

rubric.why: Hard-disk loading involves loading the operating system.
rubric.description: Identifies the operating system as the software being loaded.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the operating system.

rubric.why: Identifies the source from which the operating system is loaded.
rubric.description: States that the operating system is loaded from the hard disk.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the hard disk as the source.

modelAnswer: Hard-disk loading is the process of loading the operating system from the hard disk into the computer's main memory (RAM).

rubric.why: A network links multiple computers or devices.
rubric.description: States that two or more computers are connected.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the connected computers.

rubric.description: States a purpose of connecting the computers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning sharing or communication.

modelAnswer: A computer network is a group of two or more computers connected to communicate and share data or resources.

items.followUp: What is meant by a communication protocol?

rubric.why: A protocol is a defined set of rules or standards.
rubric.description: Identifies a protocol as rules or standards.

rubric.why: The rules govern communication or data exchange between devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the rules to communication or data exchange.

modelAnswer: A protocol is a set of rules that governs communication and the exchange of data between devices on a network.
